title: feat(brightness): lower brightness with hyprsunset
head: fd986e12139a
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Hyprsunset's real gamma reply has six decimal places; set and cleanup compare it with integer strings
leads.consequence: A request for 0% changes the backlight to zero and sets gamma to 25, but times out with exit 1 after ten verification attempts; a request for 1% from that state sets gamma to 100 but times out before restoring the backlight, leaving hardware at zero. Querying the hardware-zero handoff can still show a gamma-derived value. Cleanup also refuses a real '100.000000' reply, so the brightness-owned process/state can persist after other routes restore gamma.
leads.triage: refuted; hyprsunset v0.4.0 builds with CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 26 (coordinator verified CMakeLists.txt:46); Opus compiled the arithmetic with gnu++26 and got bare integers; the PR's string comparison matches. Kept only as private robustness note (Opus N1).

leads.summary: Open PR #13332 defines a competing gamma_brightness and writes the same global gamma for DDC-less displays
leads.consequence: If both PRs are manually merged without reconciling their two gamma_brightness definitions, whichever definition wins makes one branch's query scale wrong: the internal 0%-backlight branch would report gamma 25..100 as brightness instead of 0.0..1.0, or the unsupported-external fallback would report 0.0..1.0 instead of its intended 20..100. Even after resolving the name collision, setting an unsupported external to e.g. 50% gamma is undone by a subsequent internal hardware brightness change, which sends gamma=100 globally; an internal subpercent change dims that external in turn. Both PRs' separate mocked tests do not cover this combination.
leads.triage: published; Coordinator verified #13332 open, same file, own gamma_brightness via public diff; Opus self-check confirmed; published as Related open PR note (F11 wording fix applied).

leads.summary: Cleanup treats any one-profile hyprsunset.conf as a disposable identity config
leads.consequence: If a user has configured one scheduled profile (documented as a supported night-light configuration) and the brightness helper starts hyprsunset, returning the hardware backlight above zero while temperature is at least 6000 and gamma is 100 kills that schedule's process. There is no profile timer until hyprsunset is started again; the one-profile configuration is not necessarily the stock identity-only profile.
leads.triage: not_published; Manual does document a single time profile, but it pairs it with autostart, so the process is not brightness-owned; the kill needs brightness to have started hyprsunset first and temperature >= 6000. Narrow; dropped.

leads.summary: The global newest hyprsunset PID is not proof that it owns the current session's IPC process
leads.consequence: With two Hyprland sessions or a second hyprsunset instance, starting brightness's daemon can record another session's newer PID; a later cleanup can kill that unrelated process when the state file still matches pgrep's newest PID. Conversely, if brightness's daemon is no longer the globally newest process, cleanup discards its state without stopping it, even though its own IPC gamma can be reset to 100. The new test substitutes a single-PID pgrep and never covers this boundary.
leads.triage: corroborates_opus; Same unscoped pgrep as Opus finding 4; published via its pgrep -u suggestion.

leads.summary: Missing fourth brightnessctl -m field is silently presented as a valid 1.0% brightness
leads.consequence: If brightnessctl emits a record without its percentage field, awk sets found=1 and prints an empty value, the shell evaluates empty hardware as zero, and the query returns 1.0 when no hyprsunset is running. The monitor panel keeps the brightness slider visible and advertises 1.0% even though the current hardware percentage is unknown. This is a malformed-output boundary, not a claim that ordinary brightnessctl omits this field.
leads.triage: not_published; Malformed brightnessctl output edge case, not normal behaviour; dropped.

limits: No real desktop, installed backlight, hyprsunset process or host socket was inspected or signalled. All executed PR code ran in sealed review.py sandboxes with private stubs; upstream IPC formatting was validated from v0.4.0 source and a six-decimal stub, not a live compositor.

The repository's package list names hyprsunset without pinning a version (install/omarchy-base.packages:58); upstream v0.4.0 has the same to_string behavior as the August 2026 source examined. This change creates no system user/group or new package ID, so sysusers collision checks do not apply.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in a sandbox with stubs modelled on hyprsunset v0.4.0 IPC and brightnessctl 0.5.x arithmetic, the brightness keys on an internal panel step down from 2% to 1%, then to hardware 0 (reported `1.0`), then through ten gamma steps (`93, 85, 78, 70, 63, 55, 48, 40, 33, 25`, reported `0.9` to `0.0`). The `+` keys retrace the same steps. With night light off and at most one profile in `hyprsunset.conf`, the hyprsunset started by the brightness script is stopped again once gamma returns to 100%. The new test passes on this head and fails on the base scripts.

The main concerns are at the edges: the 1% backlight floor is gone, gamma also dims external monitors, the monitor panel steps unevenly around 1%, and normal-range brightness changes now reset any hyprsunset gamma.

### Default keys and the panel now write raw backlight 0

Base clamps the down key at 1% (`(( target < 1 )) && target=1`), a clamp added in #5525 ("Ensure we don't go below 1% / To prevent screen from turning off entirely on some models"). Base also binds Shift+Down "Brightness minimum" to `1%`. The PR removes both limits: the down key steps to 0, `media.lua` binds Shift+Down to `0%`, every absolute value below 1% runs `brightnessctl set 0%`, and the internal slider minimum is now 0. brightnessctl's default minimum is raw 0, so `set 0%` writes raw 0.

Sandbox run, max brightness 255, starting at raw 3 (1%):

| Action | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `5%-` at 1% | raw stays 3 | raw 0, OSD `1.0` |
| Shift+Down | `1%` → raw 3 | `0%` → raw 0, gamma 25 |

On base, the precise down key (`1%-`) could already reach raw 0. The PR moves the plain down key, the minimum shortcut and the panel onto that path.

**Impact:** on panels whose backlight turns off at raw 0 (the case #5525 guarded against, also described in systemd's `src/backlight/backlight.c`), the first press below 1% blanks the screen while the OSD shows `1.0%`, and the ten gamma steps are not visible. Getting back from the minimum takes 11 presses of the up key (Shift+Up jumps straight to 100%). The bindings are `locked = true`, so this also applies at the lock screen. Not reproduced on physical hardware.

**Suggested change:** keep the backlight at its existing 1% floor and apply the gamma steps on top of it, or make raw 0 opt-in.

### Gamma dims external monitors too, with no way back from them

hyprsunset builds one colour matrix (`src/Hyprsunset.cpp:93-94`) and applies it to every bound output in `reload()`. v0.4.0 has no per-output option. The Apple and DDC branches of `omarchy-brightness-display` never touch gamma, and the external panel slider keeps its minimum of 1.

Sandbox run:

```text
internal eDP-1: 0%           -> gamma 25, brightness-owned hyprsunset running
focus DP-1:     +5%, +5%     -> DDC stub only, gamma stays 25
focus DP-1:     100%, 80%    -> DDC stub only, gamma stays 25
```

**Impact:** dimming the laptop below 1% also dims connected external monitors down to 25% gamma. After focus moves to an external monitor, or the lid closes in clamshell mode, the keys and panel only adjust DDC, and the picture stays dimmed until brightness is raised on the internal panel again, hyprsunset restarts, or hyprsunset re-applies its configured profile at the profile's time (07:00 in the shipped config). This differs from the description's "External display brightness behavior is unchanged".

**Suggested change:** one option is to reset gamma to 100% when an Apple or DDC display is adjusted. Because gamma is global, this also lifts the internal panel back to the `1.0` level, so the trade-off is worth stating in the code or docs. The script only runs on key presses, so it cannot react to focus changes by itself.

### Monitor panel sticks at 1% going up and jumps to the minimum going down

In `Panel.qml`, the keyboard handler and the bar-icon wheel use a 0.1 step whenever `brightnessPercent <= 1`, otherwise the full step. `Model.clampBrightness` rounds values of 1 or more to integers, so `1 + 0.1` rounds back to `1`. Going down, the full step is not clamped at 1 before entering the sub-1% range.

Results from a Node harness that loads the pinned `Model.js` and copies the Panel expressions verbatim (internal `eDP-1`):

| Start | Action | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `l` five times | `1` → `1, 1, 1, 1, 1` |
| 0.8 | `l` five times | `0.8` → `0.9, 1, 1, 1, 1` |
| 2 to 5 | `h` once | `0` (sends `0%`: hardware 0 plus gamma 25) |
| 3 | bar scroll down | `0` |

External monitors are unaffected (`l` from 1 on `DP-1` gives `1, 6, 11`). QML was not run in Quickshell.

**Impact:** on internal displays, keyboard `l` and bar scroll-up cannot leave 1%, and one step down from 2 to 5% goes straight to the darkest level.

**Suggested change:** use the 0.1 step only when going down from 1 or less, or up from below 1. When stepping down from above 1, stop at 1 first.

### Normal-range brightness changes reset hyprsunset gamma and depend on its IPC

After every step at hardware above 0, and before every absolute set of 1% or more, the script now runs `omarchy-brightness-display-gamma set 100` and exits on failure. `set` runs whenever `pgrep -n -x hyprsunset` finds any hyprsunset, not only one the script started, and makes up to 10 attempts 0.2 s apart before failing.

Sandbox run with hyprsunset started outside the script (profile gamma 0.8, backlight at 50%):

| Action | Base gamma | This PR gamma |
|---|---|---|
| `+5%` | 80 | 100 |
| `5%-` | 80 | 100 |
| `40%` | 80 | 100 |

**Impact:** a gamma the user set through `hyprsunset.conf`, `-g` or `hyprctl hyprsunset gamma` is overwritten by the next brightness key press. Brightness keys also now depend on hyprsunset IPC at every level: when `pgrep` sees a hyprsunset whose IPC does not answer (simulated in the sandbox), each normal-range key press exits 1 after about 2 s with no OSD, absolute sets leave the backlight unchanged because the gamma reset runs first, and at hardware 0 the keys fail immediately and brightness stays at 0.

**Suggested change:** record in the state file when this script lowers gamma, and reset to 100 only while that record exists. Also scope `pgrep` to the current user (`pgrep -u "$UID"`), and don't abort a hardware brightness change when the gamma reset fails.

**Night light note:** a hyprsunset started by the brightness script loads the shipped identity profile at 6000 K. `omarchy-toggle-nightlight` only turns night light on from an empty value or 6500, so after dimming below 1% the first Super+Ctrl+N press sets 6500 and only the second gives 4000 (sandbox run). Base already behaves this way when hyprsunset is autostarted, which Omarchy does not do by default.

**Related open PR:** #13332 ("Fall back to hyprsunset gamma on displays without DDC/CI") also changes `bin/omarchy-brightness-display`. It defines its own `gamma_brightness` function, which returns hyprsunset's current gamma as an integer percentage (its writes are clamped to 20 to 100), while this PR's function returns 0.0 to 1.0. Since hyprsunset gamma applies to every output, the two features would also overwrite each other's gamma if both were merged.

**Optional test improvement:** in `test/shell.d/brightness-display-gamma-test.sh`, replacing the PID ownership check in `owned_pid()` (`[[ $(running_pid) == "$pid" ]] || return 1`), which `cleanup` calls, with `true` still passes every case, and so does disabling the multi-profile guard. The "preexisting hyprsunset is preserved" case passes because the state file is already absent, and the fixture config has only one profile. Covering the ownership check needs a case where the state file names a live process other than the running hyprsunset, asserting that this process survives `cleanup`. A case with a two-profile `hyprsunset.conf` would cover the other guard.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head plus hyprsunset v0.4.0, Hyprland v0.56.2 (`hyprctl`, CTM protocol) and brightnessctl sources. Sandboxed runs of the real scripts against stubs modelled on hyprsunset IPC and brightnessctl; the Panel and OSD logic ran in a Node harness, not Quickshell. No real hyprsunset, Hyprland, backlight hardware or external monitor was used, so the raw-0 blanking relies on #5525 and systemd's documentation. The related `test/shell.d` tests pass on head and base. In a full `test/shell.d` run, head and base had the same environment-related failures, and the new test was the only difference.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
